name: VAG MIB2 infotainment long coding (community)
vehicles: MQB-era vehicles with a MIB2 High infotainment unit (module 5F)
author: OpenTune contributors
description: Coding-label set for the long coding of the MIB2 High infotainment unit (VAG module 5F): 118 parameters over coding bytes 0-24 (brand, car class, navigation country, speaker channels, tuner band settings, amplifier, Bluetooth, USB, display and online-feature flags). The byte/bit/option table is converted one-to-one from jilleb/mib2-toolbox (MIT); see LICENSE-MIT.txt. Read/written as UDS DID 0x0600. ASSUMPTIONS, not verified: that the toolbox's persistence byte order equals the DID 0x0600 data, and that coding writes need no SecurityAccess (a module that demands it answers 0x33 and nothing is written). Evidence: synthetic-tested (udssim and vcar read/decode/edit/write round trips with invented coding bytes); never run against a real unit. Coding a unit the wrong way can disable functions; keep the backup the write report prints.
sources: jilleb/mib2-toolbox Toolbox/GEM/mqb-coding.esd @ a8e2f08 (MIT, Copyright (c) 2019 Chillout): every parameter name, byte, mask and option label; each param's 'source' names its persistence key
